questions.stem: A 23-year-old man presented with dysuria, urethral itching, and clear urethral discharge. He had been treated 1 week earlier with a stat dose of azithromycin 1 g for NGU. He had not had any sex since treatment. Investigations: Gram stain showed 5 PMNs per oil immersion field NAAT for gonorrhea, chlamydia, and trichomoniasis were negative
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma genitalium M. genitalium should be considered in men with persistent urethritis especially after treatment with doxycycline. Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose should be administered in men initially treated with doxycycline. However, azithromycin resistance is also reported in M. genitalium. C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae are less likely causes based upon the negative NAAT . HSV can cause urethritis, but typically symptoms would resolve even in the absence of treatment. The absence of dermatologic findings makes contact dermatitis less likely.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 2 Q19

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man presented with 3 days of whitishyellow urethral discharge. He reported that the discharge was staining his underwear. He also reported pain with urination. He had unprotected vaginal intercourse approximately1 week ago. On examination, there was white discharge at the meatus. There were no genital lesions and no inguinal lymphadenopathy. Microscopy:
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Ceftriaxone 125 mg IM stat and azithromycin 1 gram stat
Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM stat and azithromycin 1 gram stat

questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM stat and azithromycin 1 gram stat Gonococcal urethritis can be reliably diagnosed via Gram stain performed on samples obtained in office. The presence of gram-negative diplococci in the setting of neutrophils is highly suggestive of gonococcal urethritis. Ceftriaxone 250 mg plus azithromycin 1 g is the recommended regimen for uncomplicated urethritis, cervicitis, and proctitis. NAAT tests should be sent on this patient, but treatment should not be delayed until results return. Ceftriaxone 125 mg intramuscularly was used to treat gonorrhea in the past but is no longer recommended. The higher dose of ceftriaxone plus the addition of azithromycin is recommended to reduce the development of resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones were recommended for the treatment of gonorrhea in the past, but because of high rates of resistance, their use is no longer recommended. (Image from Braverman PK. Urethritis, vulvovaginitis, and cervicitis. In Long SS, Prober CG, Fischer M, eds. Principles and Practice of Pediatric Infectious Diseases. 5th ed. Elsevier; 2018.)

questions.question: A man who has sex with men presents with urethritis.

parts.text: Name 4 non-viral etiologies of urethritis. In men who have sex with men, name first line treatment according to the PHAC (include name, dose, route and duration). (table: Pathogen, Treatment)

parts_raw.text: Name 4 non-viral etiologies of urethritis. In men who have sex with men, name first line treatment according to the PHAC (include name, dose, route and duration). (table: Pathogen, Treatment)

questions.model_answer:
(1) Neisseria gonorrhoeae - ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose PLUS azithromycin 1 g PO single dose (PHAC: MSM treated as a high-risk group with this combination; test of cure recommended).
(2) Chlamydia trachomatis - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days (alternative azithromycin 1 g PO single dose).
(3) Mycoplasma genitalium - azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1, then 250 mg PO daily days 2-5; moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7 days if macrolide-resistant/previously azithromycin-treated.
(4) Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2 g PO single dose (or 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days).
questions.beyond_mandell: PHAC Canadian STI Guidelines: gonorrhea in MSM = ceftriaxone 250 mg IM + azithromycin 1 g PO with test of cure; M. genitalium azithromycin 500 mg then 250 mg x4 days, moxifloxacin if resistant.

questions.question: A man presents with non-gonococcal urethritis.

parts.text: What are 4 causes of non-gonococcal urethritis per PHAC including treatment (drug route, dose, duration)?

parts_raw.text: What are 4-causes of non-gonococcal urethritis per PHAC including treatment (drug route, dose, duration)?

questions.model_answer:
(1) Chlamydia trachomatis - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days (or azithromycin 1 g PO single dose if adherence is a concern).
(2) Mycoplasma genitalium - azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1, then 250 mg PO daily days 2-5; moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7 days if prior azithromycin or macrolide resistance.
(3) Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2 g PO single dose, or 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days.
(4) Ureaplasma urealyticum - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO once is an alternative and is active against tetracycline-resistant ureaplasmas).
(Other non-gonococcal causes in Mandell: herpes simplex virus, adenovirus.)
questions.beyond_mandell: PHAC Canadian STI Guidelines supply the M. genitalium (azithromycin 500 mg then 250 mg x4 d; moxifloxacin if resistant) and trichomoniasis dosing.

cohort_answer.text: Chlamydia - doxycycline 100 mg PO bid x 7 days. Mycoplasma genitalium - azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1, then 250 mg days 2-5. Trichomonas - metronidazole 2 g PO x1 (or 500 mg PO bid x 7 days). Syphilis (not PHAC pathogen) - 2.4 MU benzathine penicillin etc. Ureaplasma (not PHAC treatment) - doxycycline 100 mg PO bid x 7 days (Plourde). Candida (PHAC tx for VVC) - Fluconazole 150 mg PO single dose. HSV (PHAC tx for non-severe 1st episode HSV genital disease) - Acyclovir 200 mg PO five times per day for 5-10 days (or 10 day valacyclovir). Non-gonococcal urethritis general: Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days OR azithromycin 1 g PO single dose if poor compliance expected. PHAC important causes: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis; other possible causes: Trichomonas vaginalis, Herpes simplex virus, Mycoplasma genitalium, Ureaplasma urealyticum; less common: Adenovirus, Candida albicans. Mycoplasma genitalium (not previously treated with azithromycin): azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1, then 250 mg PO days 2-5; if previously treated with azithromycin or suspected/confirmed resistance: moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily x 7 days; for M. genitalium-associated PID: moxifloxacin 400 mg PO x14 days in addition to standard PID regimen. Trichomoniasis: Metronidazole 2 g PO single dose [A-I] or 500 mg PO bid x 7 days [A-I]; trichomoniasis reportable in some jurisdictions; current partners should be treated regardless of symptoms.

questions.question: [image-based question: content not extracted from slide] A man who has sex with men presents with urethral discharge.
questions.question_raw: [image-based question: content not extracted from slide]
questions.model_answer: Gram stain of urethral exudate showing intracellular gram-negative diplococci within polymorphonuclear neutrophils indicates gonococcal urethritis (>95% of symptomatic gonococcal urethritis, <2% of non-gonococcal cases); more than 2 PMNs per oil-immersion field confirms urethritis. Treat with ceftriaxone 250 mg IM once plus azithromycin 1 g PO once, covering coincident chlamydia; screen for syphilis and HIV and test other exposed sites.

questions.question: A man presents with urethritis and gonorrhoea has been excluded.
questions.model_answer: (1) Chlamydia trachomatis (2) Mycoplasma genitalium (3) Trichomonas vaginalis (4) Herpes simplex virus. (Also adenovirus and, less convincingly, Ureaplasma urealyticum.)
questions.cohort_conflict: The cohort answer lists Neisseria gonorrhoeae as a cause of non-gonococcal urethritis; by definition NGU excludes N. gonorrhoeae.

cohort_answer.text: Important causes: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis. Other possible causes: Trichomonas vaginalis, Herpes simplex virus, Mycoplasma genitalium, Ureaplasma urealyticum. Less common: Adenovirus, Candida albicans

questions.question: A man who has sex with men presents with gonococcal urethritis.

parts.text: What are three indications for test of cure?
He is given cefuroxime and azithromycin and has a positive NAAT after two weeks. Give two explanations why. What specific testing is essential now?

parts_raw.text: A.  What are three indications for test of cure?
B. He is given cefuroxime and azithromycin and has positive NAAT after two weeks.  Give two explanations why.  What specific testing is essential now?

questions.model_answer:
a) (1) Persistence of symptoms or signs at any infected site after therapy. (2) Pharyngeal infection treated with a regimen other than ceftriaxone (test of cure by NAAT or culture at 14 days). (3) Treatment with a non-recommended/alternative regimen or a documented/suspected treatment failure.
b) (1) Treatment failure – cefuroxime (a 2nd-generation cephalosporin) is not an adequate/recommended regimen for gonorrhoea. (2) Reinfection from re-exposure to an untreated partner. (A NAAT should normally revert to negative within 1–2 weeks of successful therapy, so persistent viable infection is the concern.) Essential now: obtain a CULTURE for isolation with antimicrobial susceptibility testing (susceptibility testing is routine after treatment failure).

cohort_answer.text:
All pharyngeal infections; Persistent symptoms or signs post-therapy; Case treated with a regimen other than ceftriaxone, where ceftriaxone is first line; Quinolones were given for treatment in the absence of susceptibility testing; Case is linked to another case with documented antimicrobial resistance to the treatment given; Antimicrobial resistance to the administered therapy is documented; Case is linked to a treatment failure case that was treated with the same antibiotic; Treatment failure for gonorrhea has occurred previously in the individual; Compliance is uncertain; There is re-exposure to an untreated partner; Infection occurs during pregnancy; Disseminated gonococcal infection is diagnosed; Case is a child; Follow-up testing should also be considered for PID if N. gonorrhoeae was initially isolated; Women undergoing therapeutic abortion who have a positive test result for gonococcal infection, increased risk of developing PID.
Treatment failure – cefuroxime is not indicated in the treatment of gonorrhoea; Identification of non viable organism ie not active infection; Re-exposure. Culture for TOC 3-7 days after completing therapy, NAAT 2-3 weeks

questions.question: Gonococcal infections.

parts.text: Treatment of a man who has sex with men with pharyngeal infection.
Treatment of disseminated gonococcal infection with endocarditis.
Treatment of cervicitis with anaphylaxis to ceftriaxone.
What are the indications for test of cure?
Name four causes of non-gonococcal urethritis.

parts_raw.text: Treatment of an MSM with Pharyngeal Infection
Cervicitis treatment with anaphylaxis to Ceftriaxone
Which are the indications of test of cure

questions.model_answer:
a) Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose PLUS azithromycin 1 g PO single dose (cure ~90% pharyngeal).
b) Gonococcal endocarditis: parenteral ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV every 12–24 h for ≥4 weeks, PLUS azithromycin 1 g PO single dose, modified by susceptibility results.
c) Azithromycin 2 g PO single dose PLUS gentamicin 240 mg IM single dose (cephalosporin contraindicated).
d) (1) Persistent symptoms/signs after therapy. (2) Pharyngeal infection treated with a regimen other than ceftriaxone. (3) Documented or suspected treatment failure / use of a non-recommended regimen.
e) Any four of: Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Trichomonas vaginalis, herpes simplex virus, adenovirus.
questions.beyond_mandell: The full list of non-gonococcal urethritis pathogens draws on Chapter 109; azithromycin/gentamicin for the ceftriaxone-anaphylaxis case reflects PHAC guidance.

cohort_answer.text:
MSM pharyngeal infection: Don't use cefixime in MSM. Alternative: Azithro 2g po x1 + Gent 240mg IM x1
Disseminated Gonorrheal with Endocarditis: Ceftriaxone 2g IV/IM x 28 days plus Azithro 1g PO x 1
Cervicitis with anaphylaxis to Ceftriaxone: Doxy + azithro 2g x 1 dose
Indications of test of cure: Repeat SCREENING 6 mos post tx. Follow-up cultures for test of cure from all positive sites should be done 3–7 days after the completion of therapy, particularly in the following situations: All pharyngeal infections; Persistent symptoms or signs post-therapy; Case treated with a regimen other than ceftriaxone, where ceftriaxone is first line; Quinolones were given for treatment in the absence of susceptibility testing; Case is linked to another case with documented antimicrobial resistance to the treatment; Antimicrobial resistance to the administered therapy is documented; Case is linked to a treatment failure case that was treated with the same antibiotic; Treatment failure for gonorrhea has occurred previously in the individual; Compliance is uncertain; There is re-exposure to an untreated partner; Infection occurs during pregnancy; Disseminated gonococcal infection is diagnosed. Abstain from sex 3 days post tx completion, CT – 7 days post treatment
Four causes of non-gonococcal urethritis: Chlamydia trachomatis; Mycoplasma genitalium; Trichomonas vaginalis; Adenovirus; HSV; Treponema pallidum

questions.question: In a man who has sex with men with a sexually transmitted infection, list non-viral causes of urethritis to the species level with the treatment including dose and route according to PHAC.
questions.question_raw: AM 17. STI in MSM - list non-viral causes to species level of urethritis with the treatment including dose and route according to PHAC (4)

parts.text: List non-viral causes with treatment for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Trichomonas vaginalis

parts_raw.text: List non-viral causes with treatment for N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Trichomonas vaginalis

questions.model_answer:
(1) Neisseria gonorrhoeae - ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose plus azithromycin 1 g PO single dose; do not use fluoroquinolones unless susceptibility proven; test of cure in MSM/pharyngeal disease.
(2) Chlamydia trachomatis - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days, or azithromycin 1 g PO single dose.
(3) Mycoplasma genitalium - azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg PO daily days 2-5; moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7 days if previously azithromycin-treated or macrolide resistance (14 days if M. genitalium-associated PID).
(4) Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2 g PO single dose, or 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days; treat current partners.
(Ureaplasma urealyticum - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days; Mycoplasma hominis is not an established cause of urethritis.)
questions.beyond_mandell: PHAC Canadian STI Guidelines provide the MSM gonorrhea regimen with test of cure and the M. genitalium and trichomoniasis dosing.

cohort_answer.text: N. gonorrhoeae - ceftriaxone 250mg IM + 1g Azithromycin. C. trachomatis - azithromycin 1g PO or doxy 100mg PO BID x7d. Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2g x1 or 500mg PO BID x7d. Mycoplasma genitalium - Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg PO x2-5d (if previously treated with azithro, Moxi 400mg daily x7d; if PID, Moxi 400 x14d); NAAT is diagnostic test of choice, routine screening not recommended. Ureaplasma urealyticum - doxycycline 100mg PO BID x7 days (no PHAC guideline; Sanford: doxy or azithro 1g x1).
